title: check, init's plan and threads only read GitHub; init changes the swerepo ruleset and merge settings only after a yes
assertion: With a repository on GitHub and `gh` logged in (a fake `gh` that logs every call and its request body), `swerepo check` (text and `--json`, before and after the ruleset files exist), `swerepo init --dry-run` and `swerepo threads` only read: REST calls use GET only, and GraphQL sends a query, never a mutation (in its arguments or on stdin, with `--input -` or `--input=-`). Every other `gh` call counts as a change, however it is spelled: `-X PUT`, `-XPUT`, `--method PUT`, `--method=PUT`, or a body (`-f`, `-F`, `--field`, `--raw-field`, `--input`, attached or not) with no method. `swerepo check --ci` doesn't call `gh` at all, with or without the ruleset files. `swerepo init --only github` changes nothing on GitHub: without `--yes` and without a terminal, when the person says no at "Apply?", or when they are asked about the ruleset and the merge settings and say no to both. With `--yes` it changes only the repository's merge settings and the ruleset named `swerepo`: it updates that ruleset in place, or creates it when there is none, and never touches another ruleset. What it sends is exactly the committed `ruleset.json` and `repo-settings.json`.

origin.text: ADR-20261123-4e40 (Phase 5): check is read-only and never needs GitHub in CI (spec §15); threads only reads (spec §17); init shows the ruleset and settings first and changes GitHub only after the person's yes, never touching other rulesets (spec §12). Tightened at the owner's request before locking: request bodies equal the committed files, check --json and --ci after the files exist, saying no in a terminal, and attached or = spellings of methods, bodies and GraphQL mutations. Tightened again after SeamSpec's reviewer: the fake gh logs stdin for --input=- too, a mutation goes through the fake both ways, and the terminal test sees both GitHub questions asked.
